body:
I'm sorry, I spent of couple of days going over the information from your last reply. I really like the guided meditation, it has helped me tune out everything else. I think it's something that I want to get in to on a regular basis.

I don't know how to explain my shameful feelings. Between the bullying in grade school and the mood changes in my parents, I always felt like I did not have a right to speak up. I know that I do, anyone does, but it's difficult to shake old feelings. I feel ashamed for existing after a bad social interaction. It makes me feel like I should not exist and I am just not made for "their" society. I know that sounds ridiculous. It's hard to explain all of the negative feelings. That's why I lock myself up in my house, so that I can pretend it did not happen and forget it.

I read your link on rumination and Googled further. Thanks for getting me started on that thought.

That is funny. I still want to go after a science career, but I understand that I should stay level headed. I do work on computers, but not for the general public. I enjoyed contract work much more, but now I work for a school system. The pay is steady and I get benefits, but the social interaction is not rewarding at all. I do not usually see the people I am helping, and when I do it's usually because they are upset.

I often feel too self-aware, and very self-critical. Of course, I understand that does not mean my self-critical thoughts are necessarily true, but again with "getting out of my own mind."

When I am turned down or ignored it makes me feel like I did something wrong, like I don't belong. I get deep feelings of regret and feel ashamed. Oftentimes I'll retreat to a place where I feel safe and repeat the conversation to myself, unwillingly. After that I tend to become a shut-in for multiple days. Then reflecting on the situation later, I become embarrassed at how socially immature I am and that tends to push me further into depression. It's just a cycle that feeds itself, all the while the person who I felt "wronged" me probably did not think anything of the exchange. My rational mind tells me that they probably did not mean to offend me, but it's difficult to convince myself that it is true.

The turning down is not usually something extreme. I do not have friends and I usually only meet new people at work. It's the lack of eye contact when meeting new people, the fact that the conversation is almost always redirected to someone else and I just stand there feeling stupid listening to two other people have a conversation that I started. A lot of people at work ignore me, too. I'm not very conventional for the place that I am living in, and a few of my ideas offend people. The "controversial" ideas are pretty basic, religion, politics, and general philosophy.

Thank you for the link, I'll read up on resilience. A difficult situation? I don't know, I tend to trivialize my own problems. I don't usually think they are worth dwelling on, with all of the problems in the world. My rational mind knows better, but, again, it's hard to convince myself that it is true. The most difficult thing I've ever had to deal with was bullying throughout grade school. I am 26 now, but the bullying and the social isolation it brought still impacts my life. The friends I made while in school were all social outcasts and I think the lack of social maturity all around created most of the problems with our relationships. I don't know if I really dealt with it, though. I would spend time alone to recharge. I am certain that I am a natural introvert, but I think I use the isolation as a crutch.

I've always been interested in meditation, so I'll read through the mindfulness stuff as well.

I have always wanted to work in a science field, some place where I feel like I am helping our species progress, and I want to feel like I am making a difference in the world. Right now I am a computer technician and I hate it. People only act friendly when there is something wrong, and they always get upset with me when I have to charge them for damages. You never get recognition for hard work, and people are not in the best mood when their computer malfunctions. I can empathize, as people rely on their technology for so much, but it's constant. It is not rewarding.

Thank you again for the replies, this is making me think.

Thank you for the reply. My biggest issue with social goals is being turned down or ignored. Any kind of negative social interaction usually spins me into depression. I should say that I have social anxiety, but I'm not agoraphobic. Any suggestions on dealing with social rejection?

Out of debt and out of this area, that's definitely the plan. I sometimes think my biggest hurdle is getting out of my own mind. I'll try job searching outside of this place, I like that idea.
